name: Arianism
core_claim: The Son is a created being, not co-eternal with the Father; 'there was a time when he was not'.

name: Gnosticism
core_claim: Matter is evil; salvation comes through secret knowledge (gnosis); the creator God is inferior or evil.

name: Pelagianism
core_claim: Humans can choose good and achieve salvation by their own free will without divine grace.

name: Marcionism
core_claim: The God of the Old Testament is a different, inferior god from the loving God of Jesus; the OT should be rejected.

name: Nestorianism
core_claim: Christ has two separate persons (divine and human), not one unified person; Mary is not Theotokos.

name: Monophysitism / Eutychianism
core_claim: Christ has only one nature (divine), which absorbed or replaced his human nature after the Incarnation.

name: Donatism
core_claim: Sacraments administered by sinful clergy are invalid; the church must be a pure community of saints only.

name: Montanism
core_claim: New revelations through the Paraclete (via Montanus) supersede Scripture; extreme asceticism required for salvation.

name: Apollinarianism
core_claim: Christ's human mind/soul was replaced by the divine Logos; he was not fully human.

name: Docetism
core_claim: Christ only appeared to have a physical body; his suffering and death were illusions.

name: Ebionitism
core_claim: Jesus was a purely human messiah; the virgin birth is denied; Mosaic law is binding on all Christians.

name: Manichaeism
core_claim: Reality is a cosmic dualism of equal good and evil principles; the material world is evil.

name: Modalism / Sabellianism
core_claim: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are not distinct persons but three modes or masks of one person.

name: Patripassianism
core_claim: The Father himself suffered on the cross (a form of modalism).

name: Modalistic Monarchianism
core_claim: Emphasizes the monarchy of God by collapsing the Trinity into one person with different modes.

name: Adoptionism
core_claim: Jesus was a human who was 'adopted' as God's Son at his baptism or resurrection, not eternally divine.

name: Macedonianism / Pneumatomachism
core_claim: The Holy Spirit is not divine but a creature, inferior to Father and Son.

name: Monothelitism
core_claim: Christ has only one will (divine), not two wills (divine and human).

name: Catharism / Albigensianism
core_claim: Neo-Manichaean dualism; the material world is evil; two sacramental classes (perfecti and credentes).

name: Albigensianism
core_claim: Regional name for Catharism, centered in Albi, France.

name: Bogomilism
core_claim: Bulgarian dualist heresy: God has two sons (Satanael and Christ); the material world was made by Satanael.

name: Subordinationism
core_claim: The Son and Spirit are eternally subordinate in being or essence to the Father, not merely in role.

name: Tritheism
core_claim: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are three separate gods, not one God in three persons.

name: Origen's Apocatastasis
core_claim: All rational creatures, including the devil, will eventually be restored to union with God.

name: Antinomianism
core_claim: Grace frees Christians from all moral law; sin is irrelevant to the saved.

name: Socinianism
core_claim: Denies the Trinity, the pre-existence of Christ, and original sin; Christ was a uniquely empowered human teacher.

name: Iconoclasm
core_claim: All religious images are idols and must be destroyed; venerating icons is idolatry.
tradition_note: Most Protestant traditions agree with iconoclasm's concern about idolatry and reject the veneration of images, though they don't formally classify it as heresy.

name: Semi-Pelagianism
core_claim: Humans can initiate the first step toward faith by their own will; grace assists but does not initiate salvation.
tradition_note: Eastern Orthodoxy's synergistic soteriology is sometimes described as semi-Pelagian by Western critics, though Orthodox theologians dispute this characterization.

name: Arminianism
core_claim: God's election is conditional on foreseen faith; humans can resist grace; salvation can be lost.
tradition_note: Arminianism is condemned only within strict Calvinist Protestantism. It is broadly compatible with Catholic and Orthodox soteriology and is the majority view among Methodists, Wesleyans, and many Baptists.

name: Open Theism
core_claim: God does not have exhaustive foreknowledge of future free choices; God learns and adapts in response to human decisions.
tradition_note: Open Theism is rejected by most Protestant traditions but finds defenders among some evangelical theologians. It is broadly condemned by Catholic and Orthodox teaching on divine omniscience.

name: Prosperity Gospel
core_claim: Financial blessing and physical health are God's guaranteed will for all faithful Christians; poverty and sickness indicate spiritual failure.
tradition_note: While widely condemned as heresy or at minimum serious error, the Prosperity Gospel has significant followings in charismatic and Pentecostal movements.

name: Universalism
core_claim: All people will ultimately be saved; eternal conscious torment in hell is incompatible with divine love.
tradition_note: Some Orthodox theologians (e.g., Sergei Bulgakov, David Bentley Hart) have defended universalism or 'hopeful universalism.' Among Protestants, figures like Karl Barth are interpreted by some as universalists. Catholic teaching firmly rejects universalism.

name: Annihilationism
core_claim: The unsaved are not tormented eternally but simply cease to exist after final judgment.
tradition_note: Annihilationism (or conditional immortality) is held by Seventh-day Adventists and some evangelical scholars (e.g., John Stott). It is condemned by Catholic teaching but remains a live option in Protestant and some Orthodox discussions.

name: Soul Sleep
core_claim: The souls of the dead are unconscious or 'sleeping' until the final resurrection, not immediately with God.
tradition_note: Soul sleep (psychopannychism) is rejected by Catholic and Orthodox traditions but is held by Seventh-day Adventists and some Anabaptist traditions.

name: Supersessionism
core_claim: The church has entirely replaced Israel in God's covenant purposes; God's promises to ethnic Israel are nullified or transferred.
tradition_note: Supersessionism (replacement theology) is the historic majority position in Christianity but has come under significant critique since the Holocaust. Catholic teaching (Nostra Aetate) moved away from hard supersessionism. It remains debated across all traditions.

name: Kenotic Heresy
core_claim: The Son literally emptied himself of divine attributes (omniscience, omnipotence) at the Incarnation, making him temporarily less than fully divine.
tradition_note: Extreme kenotic theology (that Christ shed divine attributes) is condemned by Orthodox and many Reformed theologians. Moderate kenotic readings of Philippians 2 are accepted in many Protestant contexts.

name: Theopaschitism
core_claim: God (in the divine nature) truly suffered in the passion of Christ, not merely in the human nature.
tradition_note: Theopaschitism was initially condemned as too close to modalism but was partially rehabilitated at the Second Council of Constantinople (553). Modern theologians like Moltmann embrace divine suffering; others maintain divine impassibility. Status remains genuinely disputed.
